rv-be:accounting:31.note: No warning log was added: PayrollDeductionBucket.of (~l.45-52) still returns OTHER for any purpose text not in the fixed lists; by design a new deduction never blocks posting.
rv-be:accounting:31.summary: Payroll posting reads the deduction name sent by HR and puts it in a bucket by exact lower-case text (tax, tds, provident fund, adv ...). A deduction renamed in HR, for example 'Income Tax', is not recognised and is credited to the 'other deductions' ledger instead of Income Tax Payable, so the tax liability is understated and nobody is told.
steps: In HR create a payroll cycle with a deduction line whose purpose is 'Income Tax' (not 'tax' or 'tds').
Approve the payroll so accounting receives the payroll summary event.
GET /api/accounting/journal-entries for the payroll journal and look at which ledger the deduction credit went to.
rv-be:accounting:31.expected: The deduction is credited to Income Tax Payable, or at least a warning is logged that an unknown name fell to OTHER.
rv-be:accounting:31.actual: It is credited to the PAYROLL_OTHER_DEDUCTION ledger with no log line.
rv-be:accounting:31.verify: Unit test: PayrollDeductionBucket.of("Income Tax") logs a warning with the purpose and cycle id; the bucket mapping is unchanged.

posting:lost-events.note: Not reproducible from code reading. OutboxProcessor (~l.57-60) marks the row PUBLISHED as soon as outboxMessageTransport.publish returns, with no confirm-and-requeue step; publisher confirms/mandatory are configured only in AuditRabbitMQConfig. No scheduled requeue of old PUBLISHED rows with no consumed_domain_events row was found. So the safety net the note asks for is not implemented.
posting:lost-events.summary: On the shared testing server some posting events were marked PUBLISHED in the outbox but never reached the accounting consumer, so the purchase or sales document stayed NOT_POSTED with no journal. Setting the row back to PENDING made it post at once, so the data and consumer are fine; the first delivery vanished. Cause (confirms, queue binding order, or a server artefact) is unknown.
steps: On a stack, approve vendor payments in a loop of 100 (create, submit, approve), waiting 5 seconds after each.

In the database: select routing_key, count(*) from outbox_events where routing_key like 'accounting.posting.%' and status='PUBLISHED' and id not in (select event_id::text from consumed_domain_events) and occurred_at < now() - interval '1 minute' group by 1.
GET /api/purchase/postings to see documents with NOT_POSTED.
posting:lost-events.expected: Zero such rows; a lost delivery is re-queued automatically.
posting:lost-events.actual: Reported on the testing server only; not reproduced on a laptop.
posting:lost-events.verify: The SQL above returns no rows after the 100-payment loop; with no queue bound, the row must stay PENDING.

posting:retry-endpoint.verify: Backend answers; if added, call it for a NOT_POSTED document and see a journal entry appear.
